$comment: Rhymvex service packages. Canonical source consumed by web/ and mirrored in docs/business/services-and-pricing.md. The site is client-first: each package leads with the client's situation (`situation`, `forWhen`, `body`) and what it helps them solve (`outcomes`), not with a list of deliverables. `price` is internal-only: the public site leads with scope and does not publish figures. `outcomes` items flagged core are always part of the engagement; the rest are only recommended when they genuinely help. `note` is the tempo glyph shown on the card. Copy rules: no em dashes in prose, no 'X, not Y' constructions, one triad per page at most, and every absolute negative replaced by the mechanism that makes it true. DRAFT pricing, revise before quoting.

meta.note: Prices are proposed, not approved, and are not published on the site. Cards show the situation, the outcomes and the shape of the engagement; the figure is quoted in a written scope. Update here, then re-run node scripts/sync-content.mjs.

intro.heading: We don’t start with a package.
intro.headingAccent: We start with what’s getting in your way.
body: Every business arrives at a different stage. Sometimes the digital product needs engineering. Sometimes the whole platform and brand system needs building. Sometimes you need a high-velocity partner to ship features and creative on an ongoing cadence.
We’ll diagnose where the bottlenecks are, then engineer the engagement around it.
intro.primaryCta: Tell us what you’re trying to solve

packages.name: Product & System Sprint
packages.forWhen: For when your product, tools, or brand feel fragmented.
packages.body: There’s potential in the business, but the product, the technology stack and the positioning don’t agree with each other. We diagnose the bottlenecks pulling them apart and spend the next two weeks on the changes that count.

outcomes.label: Audit product, code, and brand bottlenecks
Clarify technical architecture and user journeys
Establish focused UI/UX and brand direction
Fix highest-impact system and product gaps

packages.name: Platform & System Build
packages.situation: You need an integrated system that scales
packages.forWhen: When your business needs a product and platform that works without you.
packages.body: If every new feature or asset requires another ad-hoc tool, more patchwork won’t help. What your team needs is an integrated system. We design and build the complete digital product, client platform, and production system from scratch.

outcomes.label: Full-stack digital product or client platform
Coherent design system and token pipeline
Operational workflows your team can execute

packages.name: Rhythm Retainer
packages.forWhen: For teams that need a product & systems partner, not another vendor.
packages.body: You’ve got the platform and the system. The hard part is keeping momentum. We sit alongside your team to ship features, build new tools, produce creative, and keep the system ahead as the business grows.

outcomes.label: Ship features and engineering sprints on an agreed cadence
Prioritise upcoming product, platform, and creative needs
Continuous code and design system evolution

addOnsIntro.heading: Additional support when it makes sense
addOnsIntro.body: Some projects need more than the core engagement. We’ll recommend one of these when it genuinely helps, and leave it out when it doesn’t.

addOns.name: Brand Audit
addOns.note: A closer read on what’s working and what isn’t, when you need the detail before deciding anything.

addOns.name: Design System Handoff
addOns.note: Turns the system into something your developers and internal team can pick up and use.

addOns.name: Additional Templates
addOns.note: For when your team has a new channel, or the same layout keeps coming back by hand.

addOns.name: Launch Creative
addOns.note: Campaign-ready creative for when you’re ready to put the new system in front of people.

closing: You don’t have to know what to buy. Tell us where you’re stuck and we’ll help work out the right engagement. If we don’t think you need one of these, we’ll say so. Every engagement is quoted as a fixed price in a written scope before any work starts, so the number is agreed against a defined scope. Retainers only begin once there’s a reason for one.
